title: GA4 Core - Getting Started
content: GA4 provides event-based data model. Key concepts: events, parameters, user properties. Events are user interactions tracked automatically or manually. Parameters provide additional context. User properties describe user segments.

title: GA4 Core - Events
content: Events are the foundation of GA4. Automatic events (page_view, scroll, click) are tracked automatically. Enhanced measurement events can be enabled. Custom events require manual implementation. Events have parameters for additional data.

title: GA4 Core - Conversions
content: Conversions are marked events that represent valuable user actions. Any event can be marked as conversion. Conversion tracking is essential for measuring business goals. Conversions appear in reports and can be used for optimization.

title: GA4 Core - Audiences
content: Audiences are groups of users with common characteristics. Used for analysis and remarketing. Can be based on events, user properties, or conditions. Dynamic audiences update automatically based on user behavior.

title: GA4 Core - Custom Dimensions
content: Custom dimensions allow tracking additional data points. Event-scoped dimensions apply to specific events. User-scoped dimensions apply to user properties. Custom dimensions must be registered before use.

title: GA4 Core - Data Retention
content: GA4 data retention policies: standard retention (14 months), extended retention (50 months). User-level data retention is limited. Aggregated data is retained longer. Important for compliance and historical analysis.

title: GA4 Core - Measurement Protocol
content: Measurement Protocol allows server-side event tracking. Useful for offline events, server-side tracking, and data imports. Requires measurement_id and api_secret. Events sent via HTTP POST requests.

title: GA4 Core - Data Import
content: Data import allows uploading external data to GA4. Supports user data, event data, item data. Data must match GA4 schema. Imported data enhances existing analytics data.

title: GTM Core - Getting Started
content: Google Tag Manager (GTM) centralizes tag management. Key concepts: containers, tags, triggers, variables. Containers hold all tags. Tags fire based on triggers. Variables provide dynamic values. GTM reduces code changes needed on website.

title: GTM Core - Tags
content: Tags are snippets of code that send data to third-party tools. Common tags: Google Analytics, Facebook Pixel, conversion tracking. Tags fire when triggers are met. Tags can be configured with variables for dynamic values.

title: GTM Core - Triggers
content: Triggers determine when tags fire. Page view triggers fire on page loads. Click triggers fire on element clicks. Form submission triggers fire on form submissions. Custom event triggers fire on custom events. Triggers can have conditions.

title: GTM Core - Variables
content: Variables provide dynamic values to tags and triggers. Built-in variables (page URL, click element) are available automatically. User-defined variables can be created. Variables can be constants, data layer values, or JavaScript functions.

title: GTM Core - Data Layer
content: Data layer is JavaScript object that stores information. Tags and triggers can read from data layer. Pushing data to data layer triggers events. Data layer is essential for dynamic tag management. Structure: dataLayer.push({key: value}).

title: GA4 - User Identity
content: User identity in GA4: User ID allows tracking users across devices. Requires authentication. User ID must be set via gtag or Measurement Protocol. User ID enhances user journey analysis. Privacy-compliant implementation required.

title: GA4 - Signals
content: Signals in GA4: Enhanced signals provide additional user data. Consent mode manages privacy compliance. Signals help with conversion modeling. Signals improve data quality when cookies are restricted.

title: Search Console API v3
content: Search Console API provides programmatic access to Search Console data. Key endpoints: searchAnalytics.query for search performance, urlInspection.index for URL inspection. Requires OAuth 2.0 authentication. API returns JSON data.

title: Search Console API - Metrics
content: Search Console API metrics: clicks, impressions, CTR, position. Data available for queries, pages, countries, devices. Date range filtering supported. Metrics help understand search performance and identify opportunities.

title: Search Console API - URL Inspection
content: URL Inspection API allows checking how Google sees a specific URL. Returns indexing status, mobile usability, rich results. Useful for debugging indexing issues. Requires URL and optional inspection parameters.

title: GA4 Core - Reports and Analysis
content: GA4 reports provide insights into user behavior, traffic sources, conversions, and engagement. Reports are customizable and can be filtered by dimensions and metrics. Real-time reports show current activity. Standard reports include Acquisition, Engagement, Monetization, and Retention.

title: GTM - GA4 Configuration Tag
content: GA4 Configuration tag in GTM sets up Google Analytics 4 tracking. Requires Measurement ID. Can be configured with custom parameters, user properties, and event settings. Works with other GTM tags and triggers for comprehensive tracking setup.
